newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen focusing on retail data.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen focusing on retail data.

text.p: Wall Street is expected to focus at its Tuesday opening on April retail sales data.
Sales at retail stores were down broadly in April, the Commerce Department said, partly because of weaker demand for new cars and a slower pace of department-store sales.

Total retail sales declined last month by 0.3 percent to a seasonally adjusted $212.2 billion -- the largest drop since June last year -- after a revision to show flat sales in March instead of a 0.1 percent pickup.
A consensus estimate by economists predicted a 0.3 percent drop in April retail sales overall. Excluding automobiles, sales are estimated to rise 0.1 percent.
The data are the first in a raft of economic figures out this week expected to guide the Federal Reserve in its rate decision.
